en: Netti:
The Section on Detailed Exposition (Paṭiniddesavāra), Analysis 13.
The Analysis of the Mode of Conveying Purification.
Therein, what is the mode of conveying purification?
It is the verse beginning: “When the question has been answered.”
Just as the Venerable Ajita asks the Blessed One a question in the Pārāyana:
“By what is the world shrouded?
By what does it not shine?”
“You say that craving is the plaster;
what, then, is its great terror?
“The world is shrouded by ignorance.”
(Ajita, said the Blessed One:
"Through quarreling and negligence, it does not shine forth;
craving, I declare, is its smearing."
“Suffering is his great fear.
Regarding the question, “By what is the world shrouded? the Blessed One clarifies the term as “The world is shrouded by ignorance,” but does not provide an elaboration.

Regarding the question, “By what does it not shine forth? the Blessed One clarifies the term as “Through lack of discernment and negligence it does not shine forth,” but does not provide an elaboration.
To the question, "What do you say is its besmearing? the Blessed One clarifies the term by saying, "I say craving is its besmearing," but he does not clarify the starting point [of the cycle].
To the question, "What is its great terror? he states, "Suffering is its great terror," which is a clear starting point.
Therefore, the Blessed One said: "The world is shrouded by ignorance."
“Streams flow everywhere,” said the Venerable Ajita,
“what is the damming of those streams?”
“Tell me of the restraint of the streams;
by what are the streams closed?
“Whatever streams there are in the world...”
"O Ajita," said the Blessed One,
"mindfulness is their restraint; I call it the damming of the streams."

Regarding the question, "The streams flow everywhere; what is the damming of the streams? the Blessed One clarifies the term: "Whatever streams there are in the world, mindfulness is their damming," yet he does not provide the starting point [of the practice].

Regarding the question, "Tell me the restraint of the streams; by what are the streams dammed? the answer, "I tell you the restraint of the streams: they are dammed by wisdom," provides the pure starting point.
Therefore the Blessed One said: "Those streams that exist in the world...
[Ajita, the Venerable, said: "...both wisdom and mindfulness."
"And name-and-form, dear sir—
being asked this by me, please tell me:
where does this come to an end?"
Regarding the question: "Ajita, I shall answer for you that very question which you have asked."
Where name-and-form ceases without remainder,
through the cessation of consciousness—
“Right here it comes to an end.
This is a pure undertaking.
Therefore the Blessed One said: “This question which you have asked.”
Where the undertaking is thus pure, that question is answered;
but where the undertaking is impure, that question is not yet answered.
Therefore the Venerable Mahākaccāyana said: "When the question has been answered."
The Mode of Conveying Purification is concluded.
